claim: every independent set of the unit-distance graph on F_11^2 -- every set of points no two of which differ by a vector of quadrance 1 -- has at most 28 points
vertex_index: v = x*11 + y for the point (x, y) of F_11^2, with 0 <= x, y < 11
edge_rule: two points are adjacent iff their difference (dx, dy) satisfies dx^2 + dy^2 = 1 in F_11
symmetry: variables are the orbits of sets of 2 to 4 points under V x| G0, G0 generated by the rotations by the points of the unit circle, the reflection (x, y) -> (x, -y) and the Frobenius; each variable is named by its canonical form, the least (as a sorted tuple) of the nonzero points of g(T - t) over t in T and g in G0, listed with the origin prepended and sorted by (size, points)
matrix_form: each matrix has anchors [point, sign] and entries A[u,w] = (1/s) sum_z prod_a [z+a in S]^sign [z+u in S][z+w in S] averaged over the group, expanded by [.]^- = 1 - [.]; it is presented as sum over blocks of U Z U^T with U's columns given sparsely and Z = G^T G / den^2
